CVE-2025-34086.title: Bolt CMS Authenticated Remote Code Execution via Profile Injection and File Rename
CVE-2025-34086.description:
Bolt CMS versions 3.7.0 and earlier contain a chain of vulnerabilities that together allow an authenticated user to achieve remote code execution. A user with valid credentials can inject arbitrary PHP code into the displayname field of the user profile, which is rendered unsanitized in backend templates. The attacker can then list and rename cached session files via the /async/browse/cache/.sessions and /async/folder/rename endpoints. By renaming a .session file to a path under the publicly accessible /files/ directory with a .php extension, the attacker can turn the injected code into an executable web shell. Finally, the attacker triggers the payload via a crafted HTTP GET request to the rogue file.

NOTE: The vendor announced that Bolt 3 reached end-of-life after 31 December 2021.

metasploit.name: Bolt CMS 3.7.0 - Authenticated Remote Code Execution

CVE-2026-115690.title: Apache WSS4J: Replay protection bypassed by concurrent copies of a message
CVE-2026-115690.description: Apache WSS4J remembers the UsernameToken Nonce, the Timestamp and signature of a signed message, and the ID of a SAML 2.0 "OneTimeUse" assertion, so that a captured message cannot be accepted twice. It checked whether a value had already been seen, validated the message, and only then remembered the value, as two separate steps. If several copies of the same message were processed at the same time, they could all pass the check before any of them was remembered, and all be accepted. An attacker who obtained a valid message before the recipient first processed it could send several copies at once, so that the same authenticated request was executed more than once. Where a UsernameToken is not bound to the message by a signature, the copies could carry different message bodies. The attacker needs to obtain the message while it is still in transit; a message captured after it has been accepted cannot be replayed. Affects deployments with a replay cache configured, as Apache CXF has by…

CVE-2026-133849.title: flowintel: Insecure Direct Object Reference in Task Calendar Access Control
CVE-2026-133849.description:
A vulnerability exists in the flowintel application's calendar functionality that allows unauthorized access to private case data. The task calendar queries failed to enforce visibility checks on the parent case associated with tasks. Specifically, tasks assigned to a user or belonging to the user's organization were returned in calendar views (including browser and API ICS feeds) without verifying whether the user had permission to view the parent case. This allowed users to potentially discover and access details of private cases they were not authorized to view, leading to information disclosure.

The issue affected the default task visibility logic and the assigned-only task queries. The fix ensures that case visibility is rechecked in addition to task assignment or organization membership, preventing the exposure of private case data in calendar outputs.

Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0

CVE-2026-99329.title: HID: mcp2221: always initialize and cancel init_work
CVE-2026-99329.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: mcp2221: always initialize and cancel init_work

The writable gpio_mode_enforce parameter can change between probe and
remove.

If it changes from false to true after probe, remove skips cancellation
of init_work. Pending or running work can then access devm-managed
driver state after teardown. Changing it from true to false can make
remove cancel an uninitialized delayed work item.

Initialize init_work whenever IIO is reachable and cancel it
unconditionally on remove. Keep the parameter check only for scheduling
the initialization.

The false-to-true cancellation gap was previously reported by Sashiko.
We also encountered this issue during our static-analysis research.
